group: block-list rewriting, coin-like block lengths (rule not found)
title: What is known about 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; the round rule is not found. The machine rewrites a long list of blocks of 1s, nearly all of length 4k + 3 with k spread like the run lengths of fair coin flips; each round multiplies the list's length by about 1.75. Nothing beyond the generated bounded runs is proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 65,183 cells have been visited and 49,646 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.085). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).

claims.title: Blocks of length 4k + 3
claims.text: At each visit of the left end up to step 5.2·108, every block of 1s except the first two and the last has length 4k + 3; the counts for k = 0, 1, 2, … halve at each step (2,665, 1,336, 716, 315, … of 5,366 at step 522,867,988). Observed in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: Rounds grow by about 1.75
claims.text: Between consecutive long gaps the list, read as a word with 4k + 3 ↦ 1^k 0, grows from 26 to 97, 351, 1,136, 3,508, 10,746 letters every second round (about 1.75 a round), and the step count by about 3.1 a round.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The rule of a round is the missing piece.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine keeps rewriting a long list of blocks of 1s whose lengths look like the results of coin flips, and each round makes the list about 1.75 times longer. What a round does to the list has not been worked out.

facts.text: Steps simulated from blank tape without a halt.
The length of nearly every block, with k spread like coin-flip runs.
Growth of the list in a round.

sections.heading: A list of blocks
html: Each time the head reaches the left end, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. Except at the two ends, every block has length 4k + 3, and k behaves like the length of a run of heads in fair coin flips: half the blocks have k = 0, a quarter k = 1, and so on. At step 522,867,988 there are 5,366 blocks:

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite the whole list
html: The head sweeps across the whole list again and again: a sweep to the right turns each block into a string of short runs, and the sweep back turns that into blocks again, changed. Between the long gaps when the head stays away from the left end, the list grows by about 1.75:
(letters: the list read as a word, block 4k + 3 standing for k ones and a zero). What a round does to that word is not known.

sections.heading: Not known
html: The machine stops only if the head in state F reads a 1; in 109 simulated steps that never happens. Without the round rule there is no honest estimate. The coin-like block lengths suggest a pseudo-random word being rewritten, as in the Collatz-like holdouts.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.085). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).
After 109 steps the tape spans 65,183 cells (190 left of the start, 43,143 right), with a density of 1s of 0.762.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Rewrites a list of blocks of length 4k+3, k spread like coin-flip run lengths; each round multiplies the list by about 1.75; rule not found; no halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps.
